chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What should I say when I face the Stone?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Exclaim the Greatness (of Allah) and send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny.'
He (the narrator) said, 'And I heard him (peace be upon him) when he went to the Stone, saying: Allah is the Greatest, peace be upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What should be said when facing the Black Stone during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the prophetic tradition of combining the declaration of God's greatness (Takbeer) with blessings upon the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt (Salawaat) at the Black Stone, a practice that underscores the spiritual connection between the pilgrim and the Prophet. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the Imam's role as the perfect exemplar of ritual worship, where the physical act of touching the Stone is accompanied by verbal affirmations of divine unity and prophetic lineage. This dual recitation serves to sanctify the Tawaf by linking the cosmic act of circumambulation with the specific spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What should I be saying when I face the Black Stone?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: 
‘Exclaim the Greatness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> (Takbeer), and send Blessings upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> Progeny<sup>asws</sup> (Salawaat)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I heard him<sup>asws</sup> when he<sup>asws</sup> went over to the (Black) Stone, he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: 
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest! The greetings be upon Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb who has said the following:

“I once asked Abu `Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, £ What should I say when I face the Black Stone?’ He (the Imam) replied, £ Say Takhir (Allah is great beyond description) and say O Allah, grant salawat (favors and compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause).’
I also heard him when going near the Black Stone say Takhir (Allah is great beyond description) and say, ’Peace and obedience is due for the Messenger of Allah.’”
